text: Anaplasma invades the blood and multiplies inside red blood cells in ruminants, transmitted by ticks. Signs are usually subacute and seen in cattle over 9 months old: fever, progressive anemia, jaundice, and drooping ears; imported dairy cattle can instead show a very rapid (peracute) form within a few hours. Zebu cattle show strong natural resistance to Anaplasma. Treatment: Tetracycline-family antibiotics — a common approach is a single intramuscular injection of long-acting oxytetracycline at 20 mg/kg.
caveat: The source notes Anaplasmosis likely circulates in Cambodia but had not yet been formally confirmed/identified at the time of writing, unlike Trypanosomiasis and Babesia.
